methods.description: Find the nonnegative number whose square is given, including exact decimal squares.
Find three equal factors to reverse cubing.
Identify squares of whole numbers by known squares or neighbouring squares.
Use square root for square side length and then four sides for perimeter.
Use cube root for a cube edge or equal cubes per edge; use twelve edges when requested.
Use the stated number of equal factors or a supplied power to evaluate a higher root.
Translate a given power/root fact in either direction, then complete the requested operation.
Distinguish square-side and cube-edge roots of the same numerical amount and compare lengths.
